$comment: Which photograph shows which machine, stated rather than inferred.
286 product photographs arrived on 12 August in OneDrive, print resolution, 1.72 GB.
Every one of these entries was chosen by LOOKING at the photograph on a contact
sheet, not by reading its filename — because the filenames are close enough to
is a photograph of apples with a label on them; 'DIAG_LCIJ_HR2600 384E Printhead' is
a print head and not the machine; and 'Corvus_CIJ_6400Series_printhead.jpg' shows a
print head rather than an 6400. A wrong photograph on a quote is worse than none, so
an unmapped model simply keeps the website capture it already had.
MODELS is keyed by the model string the catalogue uses, which is not always what the
photograph is called. The thermal jet is the case worth knowing: the catalogue calls
its machines 'HP 0.5"' and 'HP 1.0"' after the print height, and the photographs call
them TJ500 and TJ1000. Same machines.
APPLICATIONS is for the customer-facing quote: a photograph of this kind of marking
on this kind of material. `substrate` is matched against the profile's substrate text,
so it has to be the words a rep would type. `caption` is what the customer reads, and
it says 'a line like this' rather than implying it is their own product — these are
Axim's photographs of other people's lines, and a quote that suggests otherwise

$modelsNotMapped: 6400, 6410, 6420 and their PLUS variants: every CIJ photograph in the set is either
an 6440 on a bottling line or a print head. The 6440 shot is not used for them,
because the 6400 series cabinet is a different machine and a rep telling them apart
by the photograph is the entire point of having one.
Mark 2 and Mark 4 (impulse jet): the photographs are of the HR2600 system and the
384E and 768E print heads, which are the earlier Trident heads. Not the same parts.
E-TAMP, E-FASA: there are tamp and swing-arm photographs, but which module each one
shows is a question for somebody who can tell an E-TAMP from a High Speed Tamp by
sight. I cannot, so they wait.
CSL10, CSL30, CSL60, FSL20, FSL50: there is a good CSL10/CSL30 photograph, and no
